rules: Scale and focus by the lens: a 4 mm blade is ~74 mm wide on the sheet at 5 cm (blur 14 mm at f/16), ~25 mm at 10 cm (blur 6 mm), ~3.3 mm at the hand's 0.6 m (sharp) (derived from space table)
FLAG 'a few sharp ones': sharp blades can only stand in the focal zone (0.4-1.2 m at f/16), small, beside or behind the hand; every near blade blurred by its distance (optics)
Negative drawing: draw the darks between blades, keep or lift the blades; every blade has a beginning and an end (Sibley grass)
Sharp blades: lit edges indented with the stylus before any tone or lifted with an eraser pen; gaps 'almost black' (Sibley indenting; Wildlife Art Store)
Blurred blades: no stylus, no visible stroke; lay value then blend unclipped across the edge with a brush about the blur width; blur keeps value, no 'lighter because blurred' (Dessindigo; judgement)
Filtered grass (orange/red) prints darker than seen: sunlit blades L* 45-65, shadows and gaps L* 20-35 (Bolo filters; Photography Mad; values judgement)
Front-lit by a sun behind the camera: few glints, little translucency; bokeh discs only from glints, polygonal at f/16, light grey, few (Wikipedia Bokeh; judgement)
keep: tapering curved blades from a base
size by distance from the lens
avoid: sharp blades among the near blurred ones
